entries.reason: the release carries no command event class at all: read with tools/mach32_methods.py from the 6.1.3 armv7 cache, none of its 236 classes in the MediaPlayer image at 0x31fe3000 has a name holding CommandEvent and none of its 41 categories adds one, with a nonsense selector absent as the control; and all 236 were read and none declares this member's selector. That is a per-class answer, which is what decides a member: the release's whole-cache selector list (selectors_armv7.txt, 113981 distinct names) has a line for repeatType, shuffleType and isNegative because other frameworks declare those names, which is the trap facts/MediaPlayer/MPMediaItem.md:105 records for albumTrackNumber. A class the release does not have is new code and cannot shadow anything, so there is nothing native for it to be. This class is the public ancestor of four events the port already carries, so the chain a caller walks was missing a link Apple's own chain has. THE FIRST DRAFT OF THIS ROW CLAIMED THE PORT'S FOUR CARRIED EVENTS WALK A CHAIN THROUGH THIS CLASS, and the header says otherwise: MPRemoteCommandEvent.h at 26.2 declares MPRatingCommandEvent, MPSkipIntervalCommandEvent, MPChangePlaybackRateCommandEvent and MPChangeLanguageOptionCommandEvent all as ': MPRemoteCommandEvent', and grep for '@interface.*: MPFeedbackCommandEvent' over MediaPlayer.framework/Headers finds nothing in 26.2 and nothing in 16.4 - no class Apple publishes derives from it. The row stands on the class being public API at MP_API(ios(7.1)) that the release carries neither of, and nothing more. Apple's entry point for handing a command an event is -[MPRemoteCommand deliverEvent:]: it is on NO line of the 6.1.3 selector universe (113981 distinct names; controls prepareToPlay 1, aSelectorNoFrameworkHas 0), the 236 classes hold no MPRemoteCommand to declare it, and no file under packages/a/apple-backports/ DEFINES a deliverEvent: method - the name now appears in this family's own prose about it and in no @implementation. The port's own -charon_dispatch: (MPRemoteCommandCenter71.m:133) is reached from exactly one place, the subtype switch at :250-275, which maps ten UIEventSubtypeRemoteControl* cases; UIEvent.h in SDK 26.2 AND 16.4 declares exactly those ten, 100 through 109, with no feedback case at any availability, so no UIEvent on any iOS can carry one. MPFeedbackCommand's own row in ios71remotecommand.json has said 'never messaged by this port's own bridge, since no old-style feedback gesture exists' since it landed; this row now says the same about the event it belongs to
entries.effect: NSClassFromString answers the class and a caller-constructed event is an instance of it, so [MPFeedbackCommandEvent new] allocates a real object instead of messaging nil. It is never messaged by the port's own bridge, for the reason the row says
